elements.id-string-92: Ultrafast and coherent generation of magnons is of great significance for high-speed antiferromagnetic spintronics.
elements.id-string-93: One possible route is by exciton-magnon pairwise optical excitation.
elements.id-string-94: To date, such exciton-magnon transitions have been studied mostly by linear optical means in a limited number of conventional three-dimensional antiferromagnets.
elements.id-string-95: Here we investigate this correlated transition in van der Waals antiferromagnet MnPS$_3$ by using resonant second-harmonic generation spectroscopy, a nonlinear optical probe sensitive to the symmetry of electronic and magnetic excitations.
elements.id-string-96: Two exciton-magnon peaks are observed, in line with the exciton-induced splitting of magnon density of states predicted by a Koster-Slater type theory, indicating significant exciton-magnon interactions.
elements.id-string-97: In addition, a large linear magnetoelectric effect of excitons is observed.
elements.id-string-98: These findings provide renewed understandings on the correlation effects in two-dimensional magnets with enhanced quasiparticle scattering cross-sections, and point to potential coherent control among charge, spin and orbital degrees of freedom in two-dimensional magnets by optical means.
elements.id-string-100: Recent discoveries of two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) antiferromagnets (AFMs) \textit{TM}P$X_3$ (\textit{TM} = Fe, Co, Ni, Mn; \textit{X} = S, Se) with intralayer antiferromagnetic orders have brought antiferromagnetic spintronics to an unprecedented 2D realm with significant correlation and quantum effects \cite{Mak2019,Long2020a,Kim2018,Kang2020}.
elements.id-string-101: The N\'eel-type AFM MnPS$_3$ hosts many attractive physical properties \cite{Xing2019,Cheng2016,Shiomi2017,Takashima2018, Bostrom2021}.
elements.id-string-102: The reported linear magnetoelectric effect indicates the cross-correlation of its electronic and magnetic systems \cite{Ressouche2010}.
elements.id-string-103: Despite its potential as a superior 2D platform for magnon-based optospintronics, the efficient generation and control of magnons in MnPS$_3$ via ultrafast optical means remains a central issue.
elements.id-string-104: Magnons have been excited through the coupling between spin and intermediary excitations such as onsite $d$-$d$ transitions in MnPS$_3$ and localized Zhang-Rice excitons in NiPS$_3$ \cite{Matthiesen2022a,Belvin2021,Afanasiev2021a}.
elements.id-string-105: However, such \textit{indirect} excitation has less cross-section and is typically confined to Brillouin zone center, resulting in the magnons with relatively low frequencies.
elements.id-string-106: On the other hand, the exciton fine structures in these vdW AFMs \cite{Kang2020,Hwangbo2021,Wang2021b,Ergecen2022,Gnatchenko2011} manifest the fundamental role of quasiparticle correlations.
elements.id-string-107: In particular, the exciton-magnon coupling revealed by the magnon-sideband in MnPS$_3$ \cite{Gnatchenko2011} suggests a possible route of ultrafast photogeneration of magnons carrying wavevectors throughout Brillouin zone, by \textit{direct} pairwise photoexcitation of a magnon and a counterpropagating exciton.
elements.id-string-108: However, up to now, a fundamental understanding of the magnon properties under such pair-excitation in vdW AFMs has been elusive.
elements.id-string-109: Optical second-harmonic generation (SHG) is powerful for probing the magnetic symmetry in \textit{TM}PS$_3$ \cite{Chu2020,Ni2021,Ni2021d,Ni2022,Shan2021}.
elements.id-string-110: Using resonant SHG with symmetry analysis, we unveiled the substantial exciton-magnon interaction in MnPS$_3$, as demonstrated by the identification of two magnon bands split by excitonic perturbations, not observed in conventional 3D AFMs.
elements.id-string-111: The observed magnon splitting is in good consistency with the prediction by our theory of exciton-perturbed magnons.
elements.id-string-112: Furthermore, a large field-enhanced SHG at exciton resonance is revealed, attributed to an excitonic linear magnetoelectric effect.
elements.id-string-113: These findings provide renewed understandings on the correlation among quasiparticles in (quasi-)2D AFMs and may lead to efficient and coherent generation of multimode magnons.
elements.id-string-115: MnPS$_3$ has a monoclinic crystal structure with space group $C2/m$ (Fig. \ref{Fig.1}(a)) \cite{Ressouche2010,Wildes2006}.
elements.id-string-116: In the antiferromagnetic phase ($T_{\text{N}}=78\text{ K}$), the magnetic moments of Mn$^{2+}$ ions ($S = 5/2$) align at $8^{\circ}$ to $\bc^{*}$ in the $ac$-plane ($\bc^{*}\perp \ba,\bb$), with antiferromagnetic coupling between nearest neighbors, leading to the magnetic space group $C2^{\prime}/m$ \cite{Ressouche2010,Hicks2019}.
elements.id-string-117: The octahedral ($O_h$) crystal field splits Mn$^{2+}$ $3d^5$ high-spin state into multiple levels, including $^{6}A_{1g}$, $^{4}T_{1g}$, $^{4}T_{2g}$, and degenerate ($^{4}E_{g}$, $^{4}A_{1g}$), among others, with observed exciton fine structures for the $^{6}A_{1g}\rightarrow {^{4}E_{g}}, {^{4}A_{1g}}$ transition (Fig. \ref{Fig.1}(b)) \cite{Gnatchenko2011}.

elements.id-string-137: A bipartite AFM \textit{without} intersublattice interactions holds sublattice exciton $\ket{\text{E}^i,\bk}$ or magnon $\ket{\text{M}^i,\bk}$ eigenstates residing on a single sublattice $i$ ($=a$ or $b$) with wavevector $\bk$ \cite{Sell1967,Sell1968}.

elements.id-string-139: For Mn$^{2+}$ ions whose $d$-$d$ transitions involve a spin deviation (from $S = 5/2$ to $S = 3/2$, Fig. \ref{Fig.1}(b)), sublattice excitons derived from single-ion excitations are parity- and spin-forbidden and only allowed by weak magnetic dipole (MD) transitions.
elements.id-string-140: In comparison, a compound exciton-magnon transition with canceled spin deviations on different sublattices is simultaneously spin- and electric dipole (ED)-allowed \cite{Loudon1968,Tanabe1965}.
elements.id-string-141: In real systems \textit{with} intersublattice interactions, exciton or magnon wavefunctions can spread over neighboring sublattices, leading to the relaxation of parity/spin-selection rules and mixing of ED/MD characters.
